right so um the thing with the onboarding flow is that we ask for too much up front. You land on the page and straight away it wants your name, your email, your company, your team size and a password, and I think that is where like half of people give up. So what I would like to try is just the email first. You put your email in, we send a link, you click it and you are in. And then once you are in, you know, we can ask for the rest when it actually matters, like team size when you go to invite someone. The worry from sales is that they lose the company field, because that is what they use to qualify leads. But honestly we can work most of that out from the email domain. So I do not think that is a real blocker. The other thing is the password. If we go with links only then there is no password at all, which support will love because resets are, what, a third of their tickets. But some of the bigger customers will want single sign-on and that is a separate piece of work. So I would say phase one is email link only, phase two is single sign-on, and we leave passwords in for existing accounts until they have moved over. Does that sound sensible or am I missing something obvious?
